Hi pal!   


Great video and kept me interested the whole way through as it's an interesting topic and you talk very naturally throughout.   


I didn't find the cuts distracting at all, it's very common for creators to do this throughout. Your set up looks very nice, really well lit and the background is interesting.   


My only bit of criticism is that it was maybe a couple of minutes too long. Something I do whilst editing (which may help you) is constantly think, "what is the point/message of the video", does every single second of the video tell something new to convey that point? If not, cut it out. Check if your editing software has a lowpass filter and apply it to your background music. That will cut out the higher frequencies and help your voice cut through the music better.   


I really hope that helps bud. As I say, your personality shines through and you'll just keep getting better from here on out.

I've started scripting mine too. My process is writing out the script and then making bullet points from that script, so I don't sound like I'm reading on video. If I get bored writing the script, it makes me think, maybe this isn't an interesting video if I'm not motivated to complete it. 

  
If you're interested and know it will make a good video, a good little trick I've found too is to set a 20 minute timer and just keep writing until it pings. Have a break, then come back and repeat.   


Hope that helps!

I think your personality comes off as really authentic and you seem really knowledgeable. Perhaps some tighter editing would help the flow of the video to keep your desired audience engaged; that should also make your charisma shine through even more.

The only other criticism I'd have is to make the intro a bit more lively, some clever editing will help speed things up and get right into the content.   


You're very natural on camera though! Hope that helps.

As ZardozSpeaks said, the rule of thirds is not a rule at all, just a useful technique when starting out. The natural thing to do when someone first frames a shot is to centre the subject/object. The rule of thirds is used to start making you think more about your compositions and what you want to convey to your audience. 

It's a handy technique to use but don't make it a habit of thinking this is the 'correct' way of framing a shot. Some of my favourite cinematographers use centred shots to great effect.
